subject: Re: Ember AI cohort - one-off voucher routing / tax handling
messages:
-----Original Message-----
From: Sofia Ortega <sofia@ember.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ember AI cohort - promo concession request

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team loved Redwood's latency profile. We're finalizing cohort perks for our fall accelerator (12 teams, mostly seed stage) and I wanted to ask about a one-off promotional routing: could Ember get a mix of free sandbox vouchers + a small reserved-capacity starter credit to guarantee demo day throughput?

High level ask:
- 150k sandbox token voucher (usable in 90 days)
- $2,000 reserved-capacity starter credit applied on conversion within 3 months

We're asking because a couple of teams are doing live demos that need predictable jitter-free inference and we'd like to avoid an outage on demo day. We can sign a short mutual action plan if required. Also, can you confirm whether the sandbox voucher is treated as a promotional credit (no tax/invoice) or if our finance team will need an invoice for accounting?

I've attached a one-pager on the Ember cohort and a draft partner agreement for context.

Best,
Sofia Ortega
Head of Partnerships | Ember AI


On Wed, Sep 8, 2026 at 10:03 AM, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com> wrote:

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben: confirm whether we can carve out a hybrid voucher (sandbox + reserved credit) as a one-off and what the activation/expiration rules would be.
2) Priyom: confirm whether promo vouchers are treated as non-invoiced marketing credits or whether we need to issue a nominal invoice (Ember's finance team needs that for cost center reconciliation).
3) If legal is needed, Sofia — please share the minimum legal terms you require (NDA / mutual action plan).

I cc'd a copy of the EVP from the demo for internal context.

Laura Bennett

Laura / Sofia — quick ops note. We can structure this as a two-line concession: a voucher for sandbox tokens (150k) + a conditional reserved credit ($2k) that can be applied as a one-time invoice credit when Ember converts to a Dedicated or Reserved product within 90 days. Operational constraints:
- Sandbox voucher: issued as a promo token bucket (no SLA, standard sandbox infra). Expires in 90 days. No immediate invoice.
- Reserved credit: must be tied to a deal/commit (we'll apply as a credit on first invoice after conversion). To protect churn risk we require a short conversion anchor (email confirmation + hubspot deal stage change).

I flagged a couple of things for Priyom on tax & invoice implications below. Also recommend a soft cap: if demo traffic shows sustained production loads we should encourage them to move to Dedicated early and we'll fast-track the conversion credit.

Ben Carter
Principal, Sales Ops


On Wed, Sep 8, 2026 at 12:06 PM, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sofia Ortega <sofia@ember.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 12:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ember AI cohort - promo concession request

Sofia — quick finance and tax clarity.

Sandbox voucher (promo token bucket): we can issue this as a marketing/partner credit. Typically we do NOT invoice partners for purely promotional vouchers. For Ember's accounting needs, we can provide a ledger statement that shows the issued voucher value and redemption windows — that normally suffices for internal reconciliation. If Ember requires a formal invoice for a promotional item (some VCs or grant programs ask for this), we can generate a zero-value memo invoice with a note: "Promotional voucher — no payable amount." Let me know which you prefer.

Reserved credit ($2k): because this will reduce future invoiced revenue, we have to treat the credit as an invoice credit applied at conversion. That will show up on Ember's first paid invoice as a line-item credit; Redwood will record it as a contra-revenue. For tax treatment, this is standard commercial crediting; Ember's accountant should treat it as a reduction to cost of services. If you want an explicit invoice now reflecting the committed credit (for PO reasons), we can draft a nominal invoice that documents the agreed credit, but we prefer to apply it at conversion to keep books clean.

A couple of asks from my side:
- If Ember needs the $2k to be formally 'allocated' to a PO or grant line today, tell us the PO number and we'll attach the memo invoice.
- Provide the legal/MAP language for the conversion triggering event (email ok).

Priyom Das
Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference

Attachments: ember_cohort_MVP_summary.pdf
